messages:
vikram: Quick heads-up — bringing up a HF model (meta-mtl/mtl-chat-small) and saw a weird token-id gap after our hf->redwood converter ran. vocab size matches but some special tokens moved.
nora: ugh — gap as in an ID jump? or duplicate strings with different ids?
vikram: ID jump. e.g. <|bos|> was 1 in the HF vocab but mapped to 5 in our exported tokens, and some added_tokens entries ended up injected between core ids.
lucas: can you paste the added_tokens.json from the HF artifact?
vikram: here — snippet:
```
{
  "added_tokens": [
    {"content": "<|bos|>", "id": 1},
    {"content": "<|sep|>", "id": 2},
    {"content": "<|pad|>", "id": 50256}
  ]
}
```
vikram: but after conversion our tokenizer.def lists <|pad|> at 3 and then a bunch of new filler tokens got inserted before the old offsets.
marina: hmm — did the converter assume added_tokens are appended? HF sometimes mixes added tokens mid-namespace for legacy vocabs.
import-bot: converter v0.9.3 ran: token_merge_policy=interleave_for_compat
nora: that merge policy is risky. it tries to preserve original ids but will interleave when collisions happen.
lucas: any collisions in strings? like both "<|pad|>" and "[PAD]" referring to same semantics?
vikram: no exact duplicates, but there are synonyms and a couple of empty-string placeholders from prior training run.
marina: empty-string placeholders = trouble. they can absorb ids and shift everything.
vikram: repro steps I ran locally:
```
# export hf tokenizer
python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; tk=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('meta-mtl/mtl-chat-small', use_fast=False); print(list(tk.added_tokens_encoder.items())[:10])"
# run converter
./hf2redwood --tokenizer hf-token.json --out redwood-tokens.json
```
vikram: output showed a block of ~120 filler tokens inserted at ids 3..122 and pushed BOS/EOS/UNK to new ids.
nora: can you share the exact file diff from hf-token.json -> redwood-tokens.json? small diff helps.
vikram: uploaded to the onboarding bucket: s3://redwood-onboard/1723456789/hf-token.diff
lucas: quick mitigation — during conversion we should enforce: 1) de-duplicate by content string (keep lowest HF id), 2) map reserved special token names (bos/eos/pad/unk) to canonical Redwood ids before merging.
marina: agree. also add a post-conversion sanity test: token -> string -> token should roundtrip for a curated set of anchors (including multi-byte strings and nbsp).
vikram: adding to my todo. also saw one weirdness: chat template JSON referenced "system_message" token id 0, which after shift became a normal token and broke our chat parsing.
nora: that explains regression in the canary tests where role prefixes were attached to model output.
import-bot: canary run 1723456800 failed: chat-template-parse-error
lucas: patch idea: converter flag --preserve-special-ids that forcibly maps HF special tokens listed in config.json (bos_token, pad_token, eos_token, unk_token) to the Redwood reserved slots (0..3) and shifts others accordingly, failing if conflicts are ambiguous.
marina: please also add a warning when added_tokens contains empty content or control characters.
vikram: I'll implement the --preserve-special-ids and a validation step. pushing a branch now.
vikram: PR: github.com/redwood-inference/onboard/compare/conv-token-fix
nora: thanks — can you also drop a small unit test that simulates interleaving insertion so we don't regress?
lucas: and file an incident if any production model has chat parsing mismatches tied to tokenizer id shifts.
marina: noted. thanks for catching this early.
vikram: will follow up after CI. :thumbsup:
nora: :raised_hands:
